description:
The proposal is for a conservation appropriate retrofit of the existing Victorian timber sash windows at Flat 8, Ringwood Court, 24 Kidbrooke Grove, within the Blackheath Conservation Area. 

The works involve the removal of the existing single glazed panes and the installation of slimline 12 mm double glazed units within the original timber sashes. All existing sash windows, box frames, sash profiles, and structural timber elements are retained in full. No new windows are introduced, and no frames or sashes are replaced. The external appearance, traditional detailing, and historic character of the windows remain unchanged.

The existing windows are traditional Victorian one over one timber sash windows with ovolo moulded profiles. The proposed glazing units are conservation slimline double glazed units comprising 4 mm clear float toughened outer pane, 4 mm krypton filled cavity, and 4 mm Low E softcoat toughened inner pane, with a white heritage warm edge spacer and a 7–8 mm sightline. These units are widely used in conservation area retrofit projects and are designed to preserve traditional putty sightlines and the original appearance of historic sash windows.

To accommodate the slimline units, minor localised deepening of the existing glazing rebates may be required. This involves only a few millimetres of material removal where necessary and does not affect any structural elements of the sash. All rebates are stripped to bare timber, consolidated where required using Repair Care epoxy, and primed prior to glazing. The original sash profiles, joints, and mouldings remain intact.

The new glazing is installed using a compatible flexible glazing compound, with traditional external putty lines reinstated to match the existing appearance. All putty is finished in a traditional triangular profile consistent with the original Victorian detailing. No visible modern materials (e.g., aluminium, uPVC, or external beading) are introduced.

The works also include rebalancing of the sashes to account for the modest increase in glass weight. Existing counterweights will be adjusted or replaced as required, and new pre stretched nylon sash cords and solid brass pulley wheels will be installed. These works are internal and do not alter the external appearance.

Discreet draught proofing will be installed using heritage profile timber staff beads and parting beads fitted with brush seals. These are installed entirely within the existing frame and do not alter the external character of the windows.

All timber is repaired on a like for like basis using traditional methods. All surfaces are primed and finished with a breathable microporous paint system suitable for historic timber.

The proposal improves thermal and acoustic performance while fully preserving the historic character and external appearance of the building. No change of use is proposed.
